title: Testing Whether 'Planning-Ahead' Behavior Appears in Small Open Models

original_idea.body:
# Testing Whether 'Planning-Ahead' Behavior Appears in Small Open Models

**Problem:** A success state: 'we understand when models plan ahead internally, so we can detect deceptive multi-step planning.' Backcasting from 'planning detection', a prerequisite result is whether the rhyme-planning behavior found in Claude 3.5 Haiku is present (or absent) in small open models we can fully inspect.

**Direction:** On Gemma-2-2B or Qwen-4B, prompt for rhyming couplets and use logit-lens / circuit-tracer to look for activations of the eventual rhyme word before the line is written. Test whether intervening on (suppressing) the candidate rhyme feature mid-line changes the line ending, as predicted if planning is causal.

**Why it matters:** Whether planning-ahead is an emergent-scale phenomenon or present even in small models bears on when we must monitor for covert planning. Direct follow-up to a flagged surprising result; open weights only.

**Relevant context:** On the Biology of a Large Language Model (transformer-circuits.pub 2025) found Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyming words before writing poetry lines. circuit-tracer supports Gemma-2-2B for replicating such analyses.
